analysis.AN_Notes: Conceptual article on the presence/mediation and technique/critique tensions of algorithmic decision-making in social work, worked through case studies (AFST, COMPAS, NDIS, HEALER, Heat List) and a proposal for a practice-embedded critical-technical pedagogy. Bias axes from the case studies: race (COMPAS error rates, over-policing of African-American communities through Heat List) and disability (practitioner bias toward children with disability, NDIS scores overlooking the impact of disability); misogyny and heterosexism appear only in an enumeration, so gender is no object. Harms: unequal false-negative rates (Disparate_Performance) and risk scores from invalid correlations and assumed group characteristics or network proximity (Indirect_Discrimination). Mitigation: organisational and educational measures (mandatory human screening of high scores, algorithmic literacy, case-study pedagogy); Demonstrated because the authors use the case-study method in their own teaching and report student reasoning, without an assessment. Theory: critical theories of social power and technology, sociology of science and technology, critical race theory in the pedagogy; borderline because they frame the curriculum more than a definition of bias. Socioeconomic disadvantage appears only in a cited finding of the conclusion and in the question list, so it is not coded. AN_Population adds General_Social_Work because the pedagogy addresses social work education and practice across fields. Studientyp Theoretisch: the work argues the two tensions through case studies and sketches pedagogical pathways without designing a curriculum ('we have not answered the question of what would be considered an ideal unit design').
